name: Pentagon Hexagon Octagon
look: Four squares in a 2x2 grid on white, drawn like a geometry worksheet. Black outlines of a pentagon (top left), a hexagon (top right) and an octagon (bottom left) sit above their names. The bottom right square is left blank.
use: A pattern-break pun. After three shapes whose names end in "-gon", the blank fourth square gets a picture of something whose name also ends in "-gon", like a dragon, a wagon or something that is simply gone.
slots: a picture placed in the blank bottom right square
its punny name ending in -gon, written under the picture
examples: a photo of an old covered wagon
a photo of an empty pizza box
